Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim (In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful)

Surah al-Ahqaf

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Ha-Mim. The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise.﴾

We have already discussed the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'ah, the letters that open certain surahs) at the beginning of Surah Hud, and we have already discussed His saying ﴿The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise﴾ at the beginning of Surah al-Zumar.

The Almighty's words: ﴿We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth and for a specified term﴾.

The plural form in His words "We created" (khalaqna) is for magnification (lil-ta'zim).

His words "except with truth" mean: a creation accompanied by truth (muta­llibisan bil-haqq).

Al-haqq is the opposite of al-batil (falsehood). The meaning of His creation of the heavens and the earth being accompanied by truth is that He created them for manifest wisdoms (hikam bahirah), and He did not create them in vain, nor aimlessly, nor in play. Among the truth with which their creation was accompanied is the establishing of proof that He, glorified and exalted, is the One God who alone is to be worshipped, as He clarified in many verses of the Noble Qur'an that you can hardly count, such as His words in al-Baqarah: ﴿And your God is One God; there is no god except Him, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate﴾ [al-Baqarah: 163]. Then He established the proof that He is the One God by His saying after it: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, the alternation of the night and the day, the ships that run in the sea with that which benefits people, the water that Allah sends down from the sky and with it revives the earth after its death and disperses in it every kind of creature, the turning of the winds, and the clouds subjected between the sky and the earth, are signs for a people who reason﴾ [al-Baqarah: 164].

Thus the accompaniment of His creation of the heavens and the earth with truth is very clear, from His words: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾ up to His words: ﴿are signs for a people who reason﴾, after His words: ﴿And your God is One God; there is no god except Him﴾; because establishing the decisive proof for the correctness of the meaning of "there is no god but Allah" is the greatest of truths.

And like His words: (p-208) ﴿O mankind, worship your Lord, who created you and those before you, so that you may become righteous. He who made for you the earth as a bed and the sky as a canopy, and sent down from the sky water and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you. So do not set up rivals to Allah while you know﴾ [al-Baqarah: 21–22]; because His words "worship your Lord" contain the meaning of affirmation within "there is no god but Allah," and His words "do not set up rivals to Allah while you know" include the meaning of negation of it in the most complete and perfect manner.

Allah, glorified and exalted, has established the decisive proof for the correctness of the meaning of "there is no god but Allah," both negation and affirmation, by His creation of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, in His words: ﴿who created you and those before you, so that you may become righteous. He who made for you the earth as a bed and the sky as a canopy﴾, and so on.

From this you know that He did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except as a creation accompanied by the greatest truth, which is establishing the decisive proof of His oneness, glorified and exalted. From the abundance of Qur'anic verses indicating the establishing of this decisive proof of His oneness, glorified and exalted, it is known from surveying the Qur'an that the distinguishing mark between one who deserves worship and one who does not deserve it is that He is the Creator of others. Whoever creates others is the one truly worthy of worship, and whoever is unable to create anything is a created, needy being who is in no way fit to be worshipped.

The verses indicating this are very numerous, such as His words in the aforementioned verse of al-Baqarah: ﴿O mankind, worship your Lord, who created you and those before you﴾ and so on.

His words "who created you" indicate that the one worshipped is the Creator alone. His words: ﴿Or have they set up for Allah partners who have created as He created, so that the creation seemed alike to them? Say: Allah is the Creator of everything﴾ and so on [ar-Ra'd: 16], meaning: the Creator of everything is the One who alone is worshipped.

He, exalted, clarified this in Surah an-Nahl; for when He mentioned in it the decisive proofs of His oneness, glorified and exalted, in His words: ﴿He created the heavens and the earth with truth; exalted is He above what they associate﴾ up to His words: ﴿and landmarks, and by the star they are guided﴾ [an-Nahl: 3–16] — He followed that with His words: ﴿Is then He who creates like one who does not create? Will you not remember?﴾ [an-Nahl: 17].

This is very clear that whoever creates others is the one worthy of worship, and whoever creates nothing is not fit to be worshipped.

(p-209) For this reason He, exalted, said shortly after it: ﴿And those they call upon besides Allah create nothing, and they are themselves created﴾ [an-Nahl: 20]. He said in al-A'raf: ﴿Do they associate with Him those who create nothing and are themselves created?﴾ [al-A'raf: 191]. He said in al-Hajj: ﴿O mankind, an example is presented, so listen to it: Indeed, those you call upon besides Allah will never create a fly, even if they gather together for it﴾ [al-Hajj: 73], meaning: whoever is unable to create anything is not fit to be worshipped in any way. He said: ﴿Exalt the name of your Lord, the Most High, who created and proportioned﴾ and so on [al-A'la: 1–2].

When He, exalted, clarified at the beginning of Surah al-Furqan the attributes of one who deserves to be worshipped and of one who does not, He said of the attributes of the one who deserves worship: ﴿He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, who has not taken a son, and who has no partner in the dominion, and who created everything and determined it precisely﴾ [al-Furqan: 2].

And He said of the attributes of one who is not fit to be worshipped: ﴿And they have taken besides Him gods who create nothing and are themselves created﴾ and so on [al-Furqan: 3].

Verses of this kind are very numerous, and all of them clearly indicate that He, exalted, did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except as a creation accompanied by truth.

Allah, glorified and exalted, has also made clear that among the truth with which He created the heavens and the earth and what is between them, as a creation accompanied by it, is His teaching His creation that He is over all things capable, and that He has encompassed all things in knowledge. This is in His words: ﴿Allah is He who created seven heavens and of the earth their like; the command descends among them, that you may know that Allah is over all things competent and that Allah has encompassed all things in knowledge﴾ [at-Talaq: 12].

The lam of causation in His words "that you may know" is connected to His words "created seven heavens," and by it you know that He did not create the seven heavens and the seven earths, and cause the command to descend among them, except as a creation accompanied by truth.

Among the truth with which He created the heavens and the earth and what is between them as a creation accompanied by it is the imposing of obligation on creation and testing them as to which of them is best in deed, then recompensing them for their deeds, as He said at the beginning of (p-210) Surah Hud: ﴿And He it is who created the heavens and the earth in six days, and His throne was upon the water, that He might test you as to which of you is best in deed﴾ [Hud: 7].

The lam of causation in His words "that He might test you" is connected to His words "created the heavens and the earth," and by it you know that He did not create them except as a creation accompanied by truth.

Similar to this is His words at the beginning of al-Kahf: ﴿Indeed, We have made what is on the earth an adornment for it, that We may test them as to which of them is best in deed﴾ [al-Kahf: 7]. And His words at the beginning of al-Mulk: ﴿He who created death and life that He may test you as to which of you is best in deed﴾ [al-Mulk: 2].

Among what clarifies that He did not create the heavens and the earth except as a creation accompanied by truth is His words at the end of adh-Dhariyat: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me﴾ ﴿I do not want provision from them, nor do I want them to feed Me﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 56–57].

Whether we say that the meaning of "except to worship Me" is: that I may command them to worship Me, so that the righteous among them worship Me, because by their worship glorification of Allah, obedience to Him, and submission to Him are achieved, as He said: ﴿If these disbelieve in them, We have entrusted with them a people who are not disbelievers in them﴾ [al-An'am: 89], and He said: ﴿And if they are arrogant, then those near your Lord glorify Him by night and day, and they never tire﴾ [Fussilat: 38];

or we say that the meaning of "except to worship Me" is: except that they acknowledge My lordship, and submit and yield to My greatness, because believers do this willingly, while disbelievers yield to His compulsion and dominion, exalted is He, unwillingly.

It is known that the wisdom of testing and imposing obligation is not complete except through recompense for deeds.

Allah, exalted, has clarified that among the truth with which He created the heavens and the earth as a creation accompanied by it is the recompensing of people for their deeds, as in His words in an-Najm: ﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, that He may recompense those who did evil according to what they did and recompense those who did good with the best﴾ [an-Najm: 31].

His words: ﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ mean: He is their Creator and of those in them; ﴿that He may recompense those who did evil according to what they did﴾ and so on.

This is clarified by His words in Yunus: (p-211) ﴿Indeed, He originates creation and then repeats it, that He may recompense those who believed and did righteous deeds with justice; and those who disbelieved will have a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment for what they used to deny﴾ [Yunus: 4].

When the disbelievers thought that Allah created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in vain, without the wisdom of obligation, reckoning, and recompense, He threatened them with woe from the Fire because of that evil assumption, in His words: ﴿And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in vain. That is the assumption of those who disbelieved, so woe to those who disbelieved from the Fire﴾ [Sad: 27].

He, exalted, has declared Himself free of having created creation in vain, without obligation, reckoning, and recompense, and has denied that of whoever assumed it, in His words: ﴿Did you think that We created you without purpose and that you would not be returned to Us?﴾ ﴿Exalted is Allah, the True King; there is no god except Him, Lord of the Noble Throne﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 115–116].

His words: ﴿Exalted is Allah﴾ mean: He is freed from, magnified above, and sanctified from having created them without the wisdom of obligation, resurrection, reckoning, and recompense.

That from which He declared Himself free, the people of understanding also declared Him free of, as He said: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for people of understanding﴾ ﴿who remember Allah standing, sitting, and on their sides﴾ up to His words: ﴿Our Lord, You did not create this in vain; exalted are You, so protect us from the punishment of the Fire﴾ [Al 'Imran: 190–191]. His words about them, "exalted are You," mean: glorification of You, that You did not create this creation in vain, without the wisdom of obligation, resurrection, reckoning, and recompense.

His words, glorified and exalted, in this verse of al-Ahqaf: ﴿We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth﴾ imply that He did not create that in vain, nor in play, nor in aimlessness.

This implication is clarified in verses of the Book of Allah:
• such as His words: ﴿We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in vain﴾ and so on [Sad: 27];
• and His words: ﴿Our Lord, You did not create this in vain﴾ [Al 'Imran: 191];
• and His words: ﴿And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in play. We did not create them except with truth﴾ [ad-Dukhan: 38–39].

His words in this verse of al-Ahqaf: ﴿and for a specified term﴾ are coordinated with His words "with truth," meaning: We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except as a creation accompanied by truth, and with the specifying of (p-212) a specified term, that is, a determined, fixed time at which the duration of the heavens and the earth ends, which is the Day of Resurrection, as Allah stated in the closing verses of al-Hijr in His words: ﴿And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth, and the Hour is surely coming﴾ and so on [al-Hijr: 85].

His words in al-Hijr: ﴿and the Hour is surely coming﴾ after His words: ﴿except with truth﴾ clarify the meaning of His words in al-Ahqaf: ﴿except with truth and for a specified term﴾.

In verses of His Book, He has clarified that the heavens and the earth have a term at which their affair ends, as He said: ﴿And the earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded in His right hand﴾ [az-Zumar: 67]. He said: ﴿On the Day We roll up the heaven like the rolling of a scroll for writings﴾ [al-Anbiya': 104]. And His words: ﴿On the day the earth will be changed to other than the earth, and the heavens﴾ [Ibrahim: 48]. And His words: ﴿And when the sky is stripped away﴾ [at-Takwir: 11]. And His words: ﴿On the day the earth and the mountains quake﴾ and so on [al-Muzzammil: 14]. And other verses besides these.

His words: ﴿And those who disbelieve turn away from what they are warned﴾.

What He, glorified and exalted, mentioned in this noble verse, that the disbelievers turn away from what the messengers warned them of, has come clarified in many verses.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 46, verse 3 (part 2 of 2):

• As in His saying, Exalted is He, in al-Baqarah: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, it is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe﴾ [al-Baqarah: 6].
• And His saying in Ya-Sin: ﴿And it is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe﴾ [Ya-Sin: 10].
• And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And no sign comes to them from among the signs of their Lord except that they turn away from it﴾ [al-An'am: 4].
The verses of this kind are many and well known.

Al-i'rad ('an al-shay') (turning away from something) is to avert from it and to not turn towards it.

Some scholars said: its root is from al-'ardh (العُرْض), with a damma, which is the side; because the one who turns away from a thing turns to it with the side of his neck, averting from it.

Al-indhar (warning) is notification accompanied by a threat, so every warning is a notification, but not every notification is a warning.

We have already clarified the meanings of al-indhar at the beginning of Surah al-A'raf.

As for what is in His saying: ﴿'amma undhiru﴾ (of what they were warned), some scholars said: it is a relative pronoun (mawsulah), and the returning pronoun (al-'a'id) is omitted, meaning: those who disbelieved are turning away from that which they were warned of, i.e., they were warned of the punishment of the Day of (p-213) Resurrection. The omission of a returning pronoun that is in the accusative after a verb or a descriptive adjective is common, as is well known.

Some scholars said: it is a verbal-noun clause (masdariyyah), meaning: and those who disbelieved are turning away from the warning. Both have a valid basis.

The Qur'anic verses are rendered in English, and the rest of the commentary follows.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 46, verse 4:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: Have you considered those you invoke besides Allah? Show me what they have created from the earth, or do they have a share in the heavens? Bring me a Book before this, or some remnant of knowledge, if you are truthful.﴾

We have already mentioned, shortly before, that His saying: ﴿We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth﴾ [al-Hijr: 85] contains the decisive proof for the correctness of the meaning of "there is no god but Allah" (lā ilāha illā Allāh). And that the distinguishing mark between the one worshipped in truth and others is that He is the Creator. This opening of surah "al-Ahqaf" adds further clarification to that, for He mentioned among the attributes of the one worshipped in truth that He created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in truth, and He mentioned among the other objects of worship, whose worship is disbelief deserving of eternal abode in the Fire, that they do not create anything.

So His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: Have you considered those you invoke besides Allah﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 4], that is, these objects of worship that you worship besides Allah, ﴿show me what they have created from the earth﴾.

His saying "show me" is intended to express incapacitation (al-ta'jiz) and emphasis on their not having created anything.

On the reading where "mā" is interrogative and "dhā" is a relative pronoun, the meaning is: show me what it is that they created from the earth. On the reading where "mā" and "dhā" are treated as a single word used for interrogation, the meaning is: show me what thing they created from the earth?

What this noble verse includes, namely that whoever has not created anything in the earth and has no share in the heavens cannot in any way be fit to be worshipped, has been clarified in many verses,

such as His saying, may He be exalted, in "Fatir": ﴿Say: Have you considered your partners whom you invoke besides Allah? Show me what they have created from the earth, or do they have a share in the heavens, or have We given them a Book so that they are upon clear evidence from it?﴾ [Fatir: 40], and so on.

And His saying in "Luqman": ﴿This is the creation of Allah, so show me what those besides Him have created﴾ [Luqman: 11].

And His saying in "Saba'": ﴿Say: Call upon those you claimed besides Allah. They do not possess an atom's weight in the heavens or in the earth, and they have no share in them, nor has He any helper among them﴾ [Saba': 22].

Verses similar to this are many and well known, and we have presented some of them shortly before.

(p-214) As for His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿Bring me a Book before this﴾, we have already presented the verses that clarify it in surah "al-Zukhruf", in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Or have We given them a Book before this, so that they hold fast to it?﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 21].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 46, verse 5:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And who is more astray than one who calls upon other than Allah, one who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and they are, of their supplication, unaware?﴾ ﴿And when the people are gathered, they will be enemies to them, and deniers of their worship.﴾

We have already mentioned the verses that clarify this in surah "al-Jathiyah" in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Their earnings will not avail them at all, nor what they took as protectors other than Allah﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 10]. And in surah "Maryam" in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they have taken gods other than Allah that they might be for them a source of might﴾ [Maryam: 81].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 46, verse 7:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who disbelieve say of the truth when it has come to them, "This is obvious magic."﴾

In this noble verse, Allah, Majestic and Exalted, mentions that when the verses of this great Qur'an, which is the truth, are recited to the disbelievers, they claim that it is obvious, clear magic.

What this noble verse includes of their slander, that the Qur'an is magic, and that the Prophet (ﷺ) is a magician, has been made clear in many verses, such as:

• His statement, exalted is He, in "Saba'" (Surah Sheba): ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "This is not but obvious magic."﴾ [Saba' 34:43].

• His statement, exalted is He, in "az-Zukhruf" (Surah Az-Zukhruf): ﴿And when the truth came to them, they said, "This is magic, and indeed we are disbelievers in it."﴾ [Az-Zukhruf 43:30].

• His statement, exalted is He: ﴿No reminder comes to them from their Lord [but] newly revealed, except that they listen to it while they are playing, their hearts distracted﴾ up to His statement: ﴿Then do you approach magic while you are seeing?﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:2-3].

• His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And if you, [O Muhammad], say, "Indeed, you will be resurrected after death," those who disbelieve will surely say, "This is not but obvious magic."﴾ [Hud 11:7].

Verses similar to these are many and well known.

The commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 46, verse 8:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it." Say, "If I have invented it, then you cannot avail me anything against Allah."﴾

Here, *am* (أم) is the disjunctive (*al-munqati'ah*, i.e., the "or" that begins a new statement). We have already mentioned that it comes with the meaning of *idrab* (a turning away from the previous topic to a new one) and also with the meaning of the interrogative *hamzat al-inkar* (the interrogative particle of denial), and that it comes with both meanings together, which is the apparent meaning in this noble verse.

So *am* here conveys both *idrab* and *inkar* together, meaning: "Leave this aside, and listen to their denounced statement, since their lie is evident in it, that Muhammad invented this Qur'an." Allah has refuted this claim (p-215) in many verses,

such as His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it." Say, "Then bring a surah like it"﴾ [Yunus: 38];

and His saying: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it." Say, "Then bring ten surahs like it, invented"﴾ [Hud: 13];

and His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And it was not [possible] for this Qur'an to be invented apart from Allah, but it is a confirmation of what was before it﴾ [Yunus: 37].

Verses of this kind are many and well known.

As for His saying in this noble verse: ﴿Say, "If I have invented it, then you cannot avail me anything against Allah"﴾, it means: if I had invented this Qur'an, by way of supposition.

The implied sense is: Allah would hasten His severe punishment upon me, and you could not avail me anything from Him, that is, you could not repel His punishment from me if He wished to punish me for the invention. So how would I invent it for you, when you cannot repel Allah's punishment from me?

This meaning contained in this noble verse has been clarified in another place, such as His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And if he had attributed to Us some sayings, / We would have seized him by the right hand, / Then We would have cut from him the aorta, / And not one of you could have prevented Us from him﴾ [al-Haqqah: 44–47].

So His saying in the verse of "al-Haqqah": ﴿And if he had attributed to Us some sayings﴾ is like His saying in the verse of "al-Ahqaf": ﴿Say, "If I have invented it"﴾.

And His saying in "al-Haqqah": ﴿And not one of you could have prevented Us from him﴾ clarifies the meaning of His saying ﴿then you cannot avail me anything against Allah﴾, because the meaning of His saying ﴿And not one of you could have prevented Us from him﴾ is that they cannot prevent Him, that is, cannot repel from him Allah's punishment by killing him, if he had attributed to Him some sayings.

That is the meaning of His saying ﴿then you cannot avail me anything against Allah﴾, that is, you cannot repel His punishment from me.

Similar in meaning is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Say, "Who could prevent Allah from anything if He wished to destroy the Messiah, son of Mary, and his mother and everyone on earth entirely?"﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 17]. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And whoever Allah wills to test, you cannot possess for him anything from Allah﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 41].

What is contained in this verse of "al-Ahqaf" and the verse of "al-Haqqah" that explains it, namely that if he had invented against Allah (p-216) or attributed to Him [something], He would hasten punishment upon him, and that no one could repel it from him, has its meaning in some other verses, such as His saying, the Exalted, in "Yunus": ﴿Those who do not hope for meeting Us said, "Bring a Qur'an other than this or change it." Say, "It is not for me to change it on my own accord. I only follow what is revealed to me. Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a great day."﴾ [Yunus: 15]. That is: I fear, if I disobey my Lord by inventing against Him by altering His Qur'an or bringing another Qur'an, the punishment of a great day.

Allah has mentioned something similar of some of the messengers in other verses, such as His saying about Salih: ﴿He said, "O my people, tell me, if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord and He has given me mercy from Himself, then who will support me against Allah if I disobey Him?"﴾ [Hud: 63] and yet another, His saying about Nuh: ﴿"O my people, who would support me against Allah if I drove them away?"﴾ [Hud: 30].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 46, verse 9:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Say: I am not a novelty among the messengers﴾.

The more apparent meaning of His words "badan" (a novelty) is that it is a verbal form in the sense of a passive participle (maf'ul), so it means "mubtada'" (one who is innovated), and the mubtada' is one who originates something without a prior model.

The meaning of the verse: Say to them, O Prophet of Allah: I was not the first messenger sent to mankind; rather, Allah had sent all the messengers to mankind before me. So there is no basis for your considering my message strange and denying it, for Allah sent many messengers before me.

This meaning indicated by this noble verse has been clarified in many verses, such as:

• His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We had certainly sent messengers before you and given them wives and offspring﴾ [Ar-Ra'd: 38].

• His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We had certainly sent messengers before you to their peoples, and they came to them with clear evidences﴾ (the verse) [Ar-Rum: 47].

• His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him﴾ (the verse) [An-Nisa': 163].

• His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Ha, Mim. 'Ayn, Sin, Qaf. Thus does Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise, reveal to you and to those before you﴾ [Ash-Shura: 1-3].

• His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Nothing is said to you except what was said to the messengers before you﴾ (the verse) [Fussilat: 43].

• His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And Muhammad is not but a messenger; the messengers have passed on before him﴾ (the verse) [Al 'Imran: 144].

• His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And messengers were certainly denied before you, but they were patient over what they were denied and harmed until Our victory came to them﴾ (the verse) [Al-An'am: 34].

Verses of this kind are many and well known.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And I do not know what will be done with me or with you﴾.

The verified view, Allah willing, is that the meaning of the noble verse is: I do not know what will be done with me or with you in the life of this world. I do not know whether I will be expelled from my birthplace or be killed, as was done to some of the prophets.

And I do not know what calamities and matters will befall me in bearing the burdens of the message.

And I do not know what will be done with you: whether you will be swallowed up by the earth, or stones from the sky will descend upon you, and the like.

This is the view chosen by Ibn Jarir and other verifiers.

This meaning in this verse is indicated by verses of the Book of Allah, such as His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And had I known the unseen, I would have acquired much good, and no harm would have touched me﴾ (the verse) [Al-A'raf: 188]. And His saying, Exalted is He, commanding him, peace and blessings be upon him: ﴿Say: I do not tell you that with me are the treasuries of Allah, nor do I know the unseen﴾ (the verse) [Al-An'am: 50].

By this you know that what is related from Ibn 'Abbas, Anas, and others, that the intended meaning of ﴿And I do not know what will be done with me or with you﴾ is in the Hereafter, is contrary to the verified view, as you will see its clarification, Allah willing.

It has been related from Ibn 'Abbas, Anas, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, 'Ikrimah, and al-Hasan, in one of his two opinions, that when the saying of the Exalted ﴿And I do not know what will be done with me or with you﴾ was revealed, the polytheists, the Jews, and the hypocrites rejoiced and said: "How can we follow a prophet who does not know what will be done with him or with us? He has no superiority over us. Had he not invented what he says from his own self, the One who sent him would have told him what will be done with him."

Then ﴿That Allah may forgive you your sins of the past and the future﴾ [Al-Fath: 2] was revealed, abrogating this verse.

The Companions said: "Congratulations to you, O Messenger of Allah! Allah has made clear to you what will be done with you; so would that we knew what will be done with us."

Then ﴿That He may admit the believing men and believing women into gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾ (the verse) [Al-Fath: 5] was revealed, and ﴿And give good tidings to the believers that for them is from Allah a great bounty﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 47] was revealed.

So the apparent conclusion is that all of this is contrary to the verified view, and that the Prophet ﷺ does not ignore his destiny on the Day of Resurrection, owing to his infallibility, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him. Allah the Exalted has said to him: ﴿And the Hereafter is better for you than the first﴾ ﴿And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied﴾ [Ad-Duha: 4-5], and that His saying: ﴿And I do not know what will be done with me or with you﴾ (p-218) refers to matters of the world, as we have previously stated.

If it is said: There has been authenticated from the Prophet ﷺ, from the hadith of Umm al-'Ala al-Ansariyyah, what indicates that His saying "what will be done with me" means in the Hereafter. Her hadith concerns the story of the death of 'Uthman ibn Maz'un, may Allah be pleased with him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entering upon him, in which she said: "May the mercy of Allah be upon you, Abu al-Sa'ib; my testimony about you is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has honoured you," meaning 'Uthman ibn Maz'un. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "And what makes you know that Allah has honoured him?" I said: "I do not know, may my father and mother be your ransom." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "As for him, certainty has come to him from his Lord, and I hope good for him. By Allah, I do not know, though I am the Messenger of Allah, what will be done with me." The hadith...

The answer is what was mentioned by the hafiz Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him. He said in the commentary on this noble verse, after citing the hadith of Umm al-'Ala mentioned above with the chain by which Ahmad related it, that al-Bukhari alone related it without Muslim, and in one wording of his: "I do not know, though I am the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, what will be done with him." This is more likely to be the preserved wording, as evidenced by her saying: "that grieved me." End of the relevant point from him. This is the correct view, Allah willing, and knowledge is with Allah the Exalted.

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

(p-390) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Ahqaf.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Say: I am not a novelty among the messengers, and I do not know what will be done with me or with you﴾ (the verse).

This noble verse indicates that he ﷺ does not know the outcome of his affair. Yet another verse has come indicating that he knows his destiny is toward good, namely His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿That Allah may forgive you your sins of the past and the future﴾ [48]. The phrase "and the future" is an explicit statement of good outcome and final end.

The answer is evident: Allah the Exalted taught him that after he had not known it, and supports this with His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And He taught you what you did not know﴾ (the verse) [An-Nisa': 113]; and His saying: ﴿You did not know what the Book was, nor faith, but We made it a light﴾ (the verse) [Ash-Shura: 52]; and His saying: ﴿And He found you lost and guided you﴾ [Ad-Duha: 7]; and His saying: ﴿And you did not expect that the Book would be delivered to you except as a mercy from your Lord﴾ (the verse) [Al-Qasas: 86].

This answer is the meaning of the statement of Ibn 'Abbas, and it is the intent of 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan, and Qatadah in saying that it is abrogated by His saying: "That Allah may forgive you" (the verse) [48].

What supports this is that "al-Ahqaf" is Meccan, while surah "al-Fath" was revealed in the year six at his return ﷺ from al-Hudaybiyyah.

Some scholars answered: the intended meaning is "I do not know what will be done with me or with you in the world, of events and occurrences," and on this view there is no difficulty. And knowledge is with Allah the Exalted.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 46, verse 10:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say, "Have you considered: if it is from Allah and you have disbelieved in it..."﴾.

The response of the conditional (jawab al-shart, the apodosis) in this verse is omitted.

The most apparent of the opinions regarding its estimation is: "If this Qur'an is from Allah and you have disbelieved in it and denied it, then you are misguided wrongdoers." That the outcome of the conditional in this verse is that they are misguided wrongdoers is clarified by His saying, may He be exalted, at the end of "Fussilat" (Surah Fussilat): ﴿Say, "Have you considered: if it is from Allah and you have disbelieved in it, who is more astray than one who is in extreme dissension?"﴾ [Fussilat: 52]. And His saying in this verse of "al-Ahqaf": ﴿And [when] a witness from the Children of Israel testified to something similar and believed while you were arrogant... Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾

Abu Hayyan said in al-Bahr al-Muhit: the two objects of "ara'aytum" (have you considered) are omitted, since the meaning indicates them. The estimation is: "Have you considered your state, if it is so, are you not wrongdoers?"

So the first object is "your state," and the second is "are you not wrongdoers?" The jawab al-shart is omitted, meaning "then you have indeed wronged yourselves."

For this reason the verb of the condition came in the past tense.

Some scholars say that "ara'aytum" here means "inform me" (akhbiruni). And knowledge is with Allah, may He be exalted.

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And a witness from the Children of Israel testified to something similar﴾.

The verified view, God willing, is that this noble verse follows a known Arabic idiom, namely the use of "mithl" (likeness) to refer to the very essence itself, as in their saying: "Someone like you does not do this," meaning "it is not befitting for you to do it."

Based on this, the meaning is: "And a witness from the Children of Israel testified that this Qur'an is a revelation truly sent down from Allah," not that he testified to some other thing similar to it. For this reason He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿and believed while you were arrogant﴾.

What clarifies this is the frequent use of "mithl" in the Qur'an to mean the essence itself, as in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Is he who was dead and We gave him life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people like one whose likeness is in darkness?﴾ [al-An'am: 122], etc.

So His saying "like one whose likeness is in darkness" means "like one who himself is in darkness." And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if they believe in the like of what you have believed, then they have been guided﴾ [al-Baqarah: 137] means "if they believe in what you have believed," not in something else similar to it, according to the verified view.

This is supported by the recitation transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn Mas'ud: "fa-in amanu bima amantum bihi" (if they believe in that which you believed in), etc.

The view that the word "ma" (what) in the verse is verbal-masdariyyah (infinitive-forming), and that the intent is to liken belief to belief, i.e., "if they believe with a belief like your belief, then they have been guided," is far-fetched and its weakness is evident.

The witness in the verse is 'Abdullah ibn Salam (may Allah be pleased with him), as the majority said; accordingly, this verse is Madani within a Makki surah.

It was said: the witness is Musa ibn 'Imran (peace be upon him and upon our Prophet), and it was said other than that.

(p-220) The most apparent of the scholars' views on this noble verse is that the disbelievers who said to the believers, ﴿Had it been good, they would not have preceded us to it﴾, were the disbelievers of Makkah, and that what they meant was that the poor Muslims and their weak ones, such as Bilal, Ammar, Suhayb, Khabbab and their like, were too lowly in the sight of Allah for Him to choose for them the path in which there is good.

They also meant that they themselves had greatness and standing with Allah, and that they deserved precedence in every good, because they claimed that Allah had honored them in this world with wealth and rank, while those poor people had neither wealth nor rank, and that this preference in this world entails preference in the Hereafter.

The meaning we have deduced from this noble verse is supported by many verses of the Book of Allah, and the best way to interpret the Qur'an is by the Qur'an.

As for their claim that what they were given of wealth, children and rank in this world is a proof that they will be given the same in the Hereafter, and Allah's refutation of them in this, it has come clarified in many verses:

• As in His saying, ﴿Do they think that what We extend to them of wealth and children is [because of] Our hastening to them with good? No, but they do not perceive﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 55-56].

• And His saying, ﴿Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our verses and said, "I will surely be given wealth and children"? Has he attained the unseen, or has he taken with the Most Merciful a covenant? No! We will record what he says and extend for him of punishment an extension﴾ [Maryam: 77-79], and the rest of the verse.

• And His saying, ﴿And they say, "We are greater in wealth and children, and we will not be punished"﴾ [Saba': 35], along with His saying, ﴿And it is not your wealth or your children that bring you near to Us in position﴾ [Saba': 37], and the rest of the verse.

• And His saying, ﴿And if I should be returned to my Lord, indeed I will have with Him the best [reward]﴾ [Fussilat: 50]. ﴿So We will surely inform those who disbelieved of what they did, and We will surely make them taste a severe punishment﴾ [Fussilat: 50].

We have already clarified the verses indicating this in Surat "al-Kahf", in the discussion of His saying, ﴿And if I should be returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than this as a destination﴾ [al-Kahf: 36].

As for the disbelievers' contempt for the weak and poor believers, and their claim that they are too lowly for Allah to bestow any good upon them, and that if there had been good in what they were upon, the people of wealth, rank and children among the disbelievers would have preceded them to it, this is indicated by other verses, such as His saying in "al-An'am", ﴿And thus We have tested some of them by means of others, that they should say, "Is it these whom Allah has favored among us?"﴾ [al-An'am: 53].

The interrogative particle of denial (hamzat al-inkar) in His saying, "Is it these whom Allah has favored among us?", indicates their denial that Allah bestows favor upon those weak ones with any good.

(p-221) Allah has answered them with His saying, ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾ and ﴿And when those come to you who believe in Our verses, say, "Peace be upon you"﴾ [al-An'am: 53-54], and the rest of the verse.

• And His saying in "al-A'raf", ﴿And the companions of the heights will call to men they will recognize by their marks, saying, "What did your accumulation [of wealth] and your arrogance avail you? Are these the ones you swore that Allah would not reach with mercy?" [It will be said to them], "Enter Paradise; no fear will be upon you, nor will you grieve"﴾ [al-A'raf: 48-49].

• And His saying in "Sad", ﴿And they will say, "What is [wrong] with us that we do not see men whom we used to count among the bad?" Did we take them in mockery, or have eyes turned away from them?﴾ [Sad: 62-63].

Many have said that the men whom they used to count among the bad are the weak Muslims whom they used to mock in the worldly life, and who claimed that they were too lowly for Allah to bestow any good upon them. This is indicated by His saying, ﴿Did we take them in mockery?﴾. And the weak Muslims will mock the disbelievers in Paradise, those who used to mock them in the worldly life, while the disbelievers are in the Fire, as Allah says, ﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed﴾ ﴿And when they passed by them, they would wink at one another﴾, up to His saying, ﴿So today those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers﴾ ﴿upon couches, looking on﴾ ﴿Have the disbelievers not been repaid for what they used to do?﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 29-36]. And His saying, ﴿The worldly life has been made attractive to those who disbelieve, and they mock those who believe; but those who fear Allah will be above them on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [al-Baqarah: 212], and the rest of the verse.

**The Qur'anic verse:** ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents.﴾

Nafi', Ibn Kathir, Ibn 'Amir and Abu 'Amr read this word as **حُسْنًا** (ḥusnan), with a damma on the ḥa' and a sukun on the sin, and it is written this way in their copies of the Qur'an.

'Asim, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read it as **إحْسانًا** (iḥsānan), with a kasra on the hamza, a sukun on the ḥa', and an alif after the sin.

We have already presented the verses that clarify this verse in the surah of "Banu Isra'il" (the Children of Israel), in the discussion of God's words: ﴿Your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and kindness to parents﴾ [al-Isra': 23]. Abu Hayyan said in al-Bahr (al-Bahr al-Muhit, "The Surrounding Ocean"): It is said that "wassayna" (We enjoined) is taken to imply "alzamna" (We obligated), which takes two objects, so ḥusnan and iḥsānan are in the accusative as the second object of wassayna.

It is also said that the implied meaning is "a charge of goodness" (īṣā'an dhā ḥusnin) or "a charge of kindness" (īṣā'an dhā iḥsānin). It is permissible that ḥusnan means iḥsān, in which case it is an object: that is, "We enjoined him with them because of Our kindness toward them," so the kindness is from God Most High.

It is also said that the accusative is an infinitive (maṣdar) by implication of the meaning "We were kind in enjoining man regarding his parents with kindness." End of his words. All of these have a valid point.

* *

**The Qur'anic verse:** ﴿His mother bore him with hardship, and gave birth to him with hardship.﴾

Nafi', Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr and Hisham on the authority of Ibn 'Amir read this word as **كَرْهًا** (karhan), with a fatha on the kaf in both places.

'Asim, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Ibn Dhakwan on the authority of Ibn 'Amir read it as **كُرْهًا** (kurhan), with a damma on the kaf in both places.

Both are dialectal forms, like ḍu'f and ḍa'f (weakness).

The meaning of "His mother bore him with hardship" is that during her pregnancy she encounters severe difficulty.

It is well known what the pregnant woman endures of hardship and weakness when she becomes heavy and the fetus grows in her womb.

The meaning of "gave birth to him with hardship" is that at the time of delivery she encounters severe hardship from the pain and distress of labor, as is well known.

These great hardships which the mother endures in bearing and delivering the child, there is no doubt that her right is greatly magnified because of them, and that her being dutiful to her and kind to her becomes obligatory, as is not hidden.

As for the hardship that the pregnant woman suffers, which this noble verse indicates, another verse also indicates it, namely the words of God Most High in "Luqman": ﴿And We enjoined man regarding his parents: his mother bore him in weakness upon weakness﴾ [Luqman: 14]. That is, she grows feeble with him, weakness upon weakness, because the pregnancy, as it increases and grows in her womb, increases her in weakness upon weakness.

As for His words in this verse of "al-Ahqaf", "karhan" in both places is an indefinite verbal noun (maṣdar munakkar) functioning as a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl). That is: she bore him in a state of hardship and gave birth to him in a state of hardship. The use of an indefinite verbal noun as a circumstantial qualifier is very common, as indicated in the al-Khulasah (Ibn Malik's Alfiyyah) by his words:

*An indefinite verbal noun comes as a circumstantial qualifier frequently, like "baghtatan Zaydun ṭala'a" (Zayd appeared suddenly).*

Some have said: "karhan" in both places is a descriptive qualifier (na't) of a verbal noun. That is: she bore him with a bearing that involved hardship, and gave birth to him with a birth that involved hardship. And God knows best.
